# Official upgrade v0.2.19

- Base: `vendor-0.2.18`
- Target: `v0.2.19`
- State: `resolved`
- Reason: Merge the formal official release with reviewed Custom adapters, scoped subscription response projection, Gemini catalog filtering and regenerated Ent/Wire output.
- Custom base commit: `1f9a78a46a6d035a0513ead0615a2b43dd40d208`
- Official target commit: `dece26153621959ccd7635814f4b2d08304e681a`
- Upgrade branch: `upgrade/v0.2.19`

## Review summary

- Shared history at `ac1b8f1271be0d674fa6f074403c1410f30a3a81`; normal merge of the isolated official Tag, not unreleased upstream/main.
- Official delta: 259 files, 22,597 additions and 650 deletions. The exact overlap and shadow source lists follow below.
- Three textual conflicts: documentation ignore rules, subscription quota reset and API-key snapshot version. No blanket ours/theirs resolution.
- Preserve Custom transactional/idempotent reset and apply official response projection after fresh execution and cached replay. Write-only scoped keys receive IDs only; JWT administrator responses remain unchanged.
- Route the new declared Gemini model list through existing Custom filtering, including when an official allowlist is enabled. Preserve original and resolved-model access checks on forwarding paths.
- Restore the official `ValidateSimpleModeGroupOperation` adapter required by the new scoped-key group service, without changing existing Custom group policy.
- Snapshot v26 rejects both prior Custom v22 and official v25 entries while retaining Custom pricing, minimum-balance, model-list and blacklist fields plus official `image_count_billing`.
- Re-run `go generate ./ent` and `go generate ./cmd/server`; preserve all existing Custom schema fields. Pure official files remain byte-identical to the target; retained differences are classified by the candidate-tree ledger.
- Trusted control-plane contract changes land separately before the upgrade PR; no CI bypass or workflow permission expansion.
- Trusted control-plane PR #267 is merged at `6d38618f3c51e20a515114ee8d9fcaeb296de116`; exact-head CI `40721567533` passed. The upgrade contains this main commit and uses its contracts and protected-path checks.
- The final Custom-versus-Vendor ledger classifies 671 retained differences: 72 fixed-path, 47 documentation/operations, 66 Custom backend, 184 test, 176 official thin-bridge, 64 generated and 62 Custom frontend files. Entries bind the actual candidate Blob; new official files are left unchanged except the two documented constructor-fixture adapters and the Gemini regression.

## Database gate

Database changes are present. The automated initial report incorrectly omitted migration/schema changes and is superseded by this review.

| Official migration | Forward effect | Compatibility and rollback |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `247_scoped_admin_api_keys.sql` | Creates `scoped_admin_api_keys` with hashed keys, JSON policy/IP restrictions, creator foreign key and audit timestamps; adds nullable `deleted_at`. | Additive and idempotent. Existing legacy keys remain in settings; new key management requires administrator JWT and step-up authentication. Keep the table on program rollback to preserve revocation/audit history. |
| `248_group_image_count_billing.sql` | Adds `groups.image_count_billing BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false` and column documentation; corresponding Ent/runtime/DTO/cache mappings are included. | Existing groups default to false. Before program rollback, disable newly enabled per-image billing and verify old billing behavior; do not drop the column or delete migration records. |

The official SQL files are retained verbatim. No Custom database structure is added by this upgrade. Existing Custom migration, Ent and read-only SQL exceptions retain their reviewed scope; blobs and semantic fingerprints are rebound to the new Vendor commit.

Production preflight is read-only:

```sql
SELECT filename, checksum, applied_at
FROM schema_migrations
WHERE filename IN ('247_scoped_admin_api_keys.sql', '248_group_image_count_billing.sql')
ORDER BY filename;
SELECT to_regclass('public.scoped_admin_api_keys');
SELECT table_name, column_name, data_type, is_nullable, column_default
FROM information_schema.columns
WHERE table_schema = 'public'
  AND (table_name = 'scoped_admin_api_keys'
       OR (table_name = 'groups' AND column_name = 'image_count_billing'))
ORDER BY table_name, ordinal_position;
```

After migration, check defaults with `SELECT platform, image_count_billing, COUNT(*) FROM groups GROUP BY platform, image_count_billing ORDER BY platform, image_count_billing;`.
The write SQL is exactly the two embedded official migration files above; application startup executes them through the existing checksum/lock/transaction migration runner. Do not manually insert migration records or apply a second invented migration.

Back up PostgreSQL and retain the previous trusted Custom release before production startup. A verified dump can restore the full pre-upgrade database if required; program-only rollback must retain additive columns/tables and account for newly created scoped keys and per-image billing settings. Existing user/group deletion is subject to the new creator foreign key if keys exist.
No production database, server, credentials or runtime has been modified. A disposable local PostgreSQL database is used for migration rehearsal and scoped-key tests; this does not constitute production-data or business acceptance.
